summary: Summit of White Rock Mountain in the Ozark National Forest; an 85-foot ranger lookout tower stood there by 1936. No source says if it still stands.

access.note: Day use at the mountaintop recreation area is open year-round, sunrise to sunset. None of the listings we read mentions the old lookout tower.

visit.trail_note: A 1.5-mile loop trail runs around the rim of the mountaintop.

events.note: 1936 newspaper account, quoted on centraluslookouts, describes an 85-foot ranger lookout tower on top of the mountain
Federal survey mark description (NGS FG1928) places the mark 13 feet northwest of the southeast leg of the lookout tower, near a frame house and a small concrete block building

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the only lookout-specific sources are a 1936 newspaper account (quoted on a lookout site) and a 1971 survey description; no source says whether the tower stands today, so status is left as the record's unknown. Corrected agency field: the record's 'Ozark National Forest - 12N-28W-22' copies a land description. Location checked against NGS FG1928 (35.6896, -93.9569): the record point is within about 50 m. Elevation conflict left open: 2281 ft (1936), 2301 ft (survey mark), 2,260 ft (recreation listing). Unread leads: a Library of Congress HABS record for a White Rock Mountain water tower on FS Road 1505 near Fern (search result; loc.gov returned HTTP 403, so it could not be cached or quoted); it may be the only remaining structure on the summit. The arkansas.com page gives a Winslow mailing address, which differs from the Franklin County on record; not resolved. A Tennessee White Rock lookout (Carter County) that search returned is a different site and was ignored.
